proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true admissions lag is closer to 2–3 weeks, delay=1 may shift peaks too early, producing phase error and underestimating the post-peak tail.
proposals.rationale: Bracket the currently favored 2–3 week lag with a shorter delay to test whether rolling-split degradation is driven by over-lagging early-season rises or split-to-split timing shifts. Keeps the SEIRS family and non-fractional dynamics unchanged to isolate timing effects.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If lag varies across the season or differs by split, a fixed 2-week delay can cause inconsistent peak alignment and rolling instability.
proposals.rationale: Core candidate aligned with prior discovery patterns and mechanistic note that hospitalizations lag infections; serves as the central timing hypothesis for rolling robustness comparisons.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May over-lag the signal in some splits, leading to late peaks and degraded short-horizon forecasts around turning points.
proposals.rationale: Retain the previous best spec as a baseline; tests whether the longer end of the plausible lag window yields more stable peak timing across rolling splits for this age group.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If admissions are genuinely lagged, no-delay mapping will systematically lead the observed series, causing early peaks and poor calibration near onset/peak.
proposals.rationale: Minimal alternative observation mapping closely related to delayed_I: removes the lag to check whether the hospitalization-rate series is effectively contemporaneous with the model’s I proxy in some splits, which could explain delay sensitivity and rolling degradation.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Same as other fixed-lag specs: susceptible to split-dependent timing shifts; may overfit a particular validation segment’s phase.
proposals.rationale: Duplicate of the 3-week lag retained intentionally as the anchor configuration for comparing rolling-split consistency against neighboring delays (1–2 weeks) without introducing additional mechanisms.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Same as other no-delay mappings: likely phase lead if hospitalization is lagged; may inflate apparent fit in some windows while degrading rolling performance.
proposals.rationale: Duplicate of the no-delay check retained intentionally as the simplest phase-alignment stress test against the delayed variants, keeping structure and fractional setting constant.
